intro: Hanoi has the place where Vietnam's heritage tree list began. In 2010 the first Vietnam Heritage Tree recognition went to nine muom, a wild mango, at Voi Phuc Temple, and only one is reported alive now. By West Lake, Tran Quoc Pagoda keeps a bodhi tree planted in 1959 by India's president, a cutting from Bodh Gaya. Beside Hoan Kiem Lake, a banyan put at over 300 years shades the courtyard of the Nhan Dan newspaper, and its crown shows from the street. Many more recognised heritage trees stand in the villages around the city.
meta_description: Hanoi's old trees: the last muom of Voi Phuc Temple, the 1959 bodhi of Tran Quoc Pagoda and the Nhan Dan banyan by Hoan Kiem Lake.
question_meta: Hanoi's notable trees include Vietnam's first heritage trees at Voi Phuc Temple and Tran Quoc Pagoda's 1959 bodhi.
question_answer: Two of Hanoi's notable trees are the last surviving muom, a wild mango, at Voi Phuc Temple on Kim Ma street, part of the group that received Vietnam's first Heritage Tree recognition in 2010, and the bodhi tree at Tran Quoc Pagoda on West Lake, planted on 24 March 1959 by Rajendra Prasad, President of India.
question_context: The Vietnam Heritage Tree title is given by VACNE, the national nature association, and has been awarded since 2010. The nine muom at Voi Phuc were put at about 700 years, the age of the temple, without a stated basis. By 2014 only four were alive, and by 2021 the press reported one, a count repeated in 2025; no source says which trunk survives, so the pin marks the temple. It opens daily from 08:00 to 20:00 by its map listing. The bodhi at Tran Quoc was a cutting from the tree at Bodh Gaya, given in return for a tree Ho Chi Minh had given India, and Hanoi calls it the diplomacy tree. Its planting is one of the few recorded dates on this map, though no source says where in the grounds it stands. The pagoda is free, open daily from 08:00 to 16:00, with a city bus stop at the gate on Thanh Nien road. Many more recognised heritage trees stand in villages 20 to 40 kilometres outside the city.

faq.q: What was Vietnam's first heritage tree?
faq.a: On 1 October 2010 VACNE gave its first Vietnam Heritage Tree recognition to nine muom at Voi Phuc Temple on Kim Ma street in Hanoi. Only one is reported to survive.

faq.q: Who planted the bodhi tree at Tran Quoc Pagoda?
faq.a: Rajendra Prasad, President of India, on 24 March 1959, from a cutting of the bodhi tree at Bodh Gaya.

trees.name: Voi Phuc Temple muom, Vietnam's first heritage tree

location.address: Voi Phuc Temple (Den Voi Phuc), 362 Kim Ma, Hanoi
location.neighbourhood: Kim Ma / Thuy Khue, Giang Vo ward, Ba Dinh

official_register.name: Cay Di san Viet Nam (VACNE), recognised 1 Oct 2010 (first ever recognition)

trees.access: Temple, OSM tag opening_hours Mo-Su 08:00-20:00 (OSM only, not from a temple page); entry fee not stated in any fetched source. Caretakers keep outsiders from picking fruit or breaking branches (Tien Phong 2021).

trees.verify_notes: Recognised by VACNE on 1 Oct 2010 as the first nine Vietnam Heritage Trees (Mangifera foetida, girth 2.92 to 5.20 m, height 17 to 29 m for the nine, per VACNE page and Suc khoe doi song 15 Nov 2010; eight stood in the courtyard, one across the street). Age: VACNE says about 700 years, same age as the temple; former site manager says nearly 1000; no measured basis, hence the broad range. Survivors CONFLICT: Thuong hieu & Cong luan 14 Feb 2014 says four alive (two felled 2012, three died by early 2014); Tien Phong 9 Apr 2021 and Bao Phap luat 30 Mar 2025 say only one old muom is alive, eight died after 2013-14 despite treatment, replacement trees planted by the temple. Alive today: ONE tree per the 2025 article; which trunk, its girth and its exact spot not given in any source, so the pin is the temple. Register only plus press; no recent photo found (lifecheck OLD, 2015 Commons). Note two OSM objects are named Den Voi Phuc: the real one is the Kim Ma way (wikidata Q10841709, heritage=2); the Thuy Khue-street one at 21.0438,105.8155 is a different small shrine. Story hook: first tree ever honoured as a Vietnam Heritage Tree, then eight of nine died within four years and the temple has been criticised for it; legend: elephant (voi phuc, kneeling elephant) temple of Linh Lang prince.
trees.story:
Vietnam's first heritage trees were nine at this temple, and within a few years eight of them were dead. On 1 October 2010 the Vietnam Association for Nature and Environment Protection, VACNE, gave its very first Vietnam Heritage Tree recognition to nine muom, a wild mango, at Voi Phuc Temple on Kim Ma street. Eight stood in the courtyard and one across the road. They ranged from 17 to 29 metres tall and from 2.92 to 5.20 metres round.

VACNE put them at about 700 years, the same age as the temple. A former site manager said nearly 1,000. Nobody gave a basis for either, so the safe statement is several centuries.

Then the trees began to go. By February 2014 a Vietnamese paper counted four alive, two felled in 2012 and three dead. By 2021 Tien Phong reported only one old muom left despite treatment, and a 2025 article said the same. The temple planted replacements and has been criticised for the losses. No source says which trunk survived, how big it is, or exactly where it stands, so the pin marks the temple rather than the tree. If you find it, tell us which one it is.

The temple is dedicated to Prince Linh Lang, and its name means the kneeling elephant. Caretakers keep visitors from picking the fruit or breaking branches. It opens daily from 08:00 to 20:00 by its map listing.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as the one old muom left among the younger replacement trees at Voi Phuc Temple. No source yet says which trunk it is, so ask the caretakers.

trees.name: Tran Quoc Pagoda bodhi, the diplomacy tree

location.address: Tran Quoc Pagoda, 46 Thanh Nien road, Yen Phu, Tay Ho, Hanoi

trees.access: Free entry (OSM fee=no; greensm.com). Hours 08:00-16:00 daily, 06:00-18:00 on the 1st and 15th of each lunar month (greensm.com, hours not from the pagoda).
trees.transport: City bus stop 'Chua Tran Quoc' on Thanh Nien road (OSM), at the pagoda. Central, West Lake.
trees.verify_notes: Cutting from the Great Bodhi Tree at Bodh Gaya, planted by Indian President Rajendra Prasad on 24 March 1959 (VnExpress 22 Apr 2016); called the 'diplomacy tree', a return gift for a tree Ho Chi Minh gave India. Greensm.com repeats 1959 and gives '65 years old as of 2024' and Bodh Gaya origin, but its photo caption calls Prasad 'prime minister', so the title is inconsistent; VnExpress and body text say President. Documented planting date for this specimen, so age is not derived. No girth or height in any source. Not a VACNE heritage tree as far as found. Young by tree standards: worth the stop for its story and the pagoda, not its size; the pagoda also has a bodhi cutting tradition so confirm on site which trunk bears the plaque (not stated in sources). Alive: 2024 article treats it as living; no dated photo checked.
trees.story:
This tree is a thank-you note between two countries. On 24 March 1959 Rajendra Prasad, the President of India, planted it at Tran Quoc Pagoda on the shore of West Lake, VnExpress reported. It was a cutting from the Great Bodhi Tree at Bodh Gaya in India, the tree under which the Buddha is said to have reached enlightenment, and it came as a return gift for a tree Ho Chi Minh had given India. Hanoi calls it the diplomacy tree.

By the standards of this map it is young, about 67 years old, and its age is one of the few here that comes from a recorded planting rather than an estimate. Nobody has published its girth or height. It earns the stop through its story and its setting, not its size.

One practical note. Bodhi cuttings are a tradition here, so the pagoda may hold more than one, and no source says exactly where in the grounds the 1959 tree stands. Look for a plaque, and if you can tell us which trunk it is, please do.

Entry is free. The pagoda opens daily from 08:00 to 16:00, and from 06:00 to 18:00 on the first and fifteenth days of each lunar month. A city bus stops at the gate on Thanh Nien road.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by a plaque for the 1959 planting by India's President Rajendra Prasad. It stands at Tran Quoc Pagoda; other bodhi trees may grow there too, so check the plaque.

trees.name: The banyan of Nhan Dan, 71 Hang Trong
trees.age_estimate: over 300 years (press figure); over 400 by a reader's estimate

location.address: Courtyard of Bao Nhan Dan, 71 Hang Trong, seen from the pavement of Le Thai To, Hoan Kiem, Hanoi

trees.story:
A newspaper has worked under this banyan since October 1954, when Nhan Dan, the Communist Party daily, moved into 71 Hang Trong about ten days after it came to Hanoi. Its own pages put the tree at over 300 years, and VietnamPlus gives the same figure. Nobody has published a measurement, but Nhan Dan wrote in 2022 that it takes dozens of people to reach round the trunk. A reader who told us about it puts it at over 400 years. Neither number comes with a basis, so take them as an estimate, not a count of rings.

The ground has had several lives around it. Nhan Dan writes that this corner of the old Ho Dinh quarter once held the school of the scholar Vu Tong Phan, and that the French later built a villa here, known as the residence of the deputy governor-general. Generations of journalists have rested and talked in its shade, and the paper recalls a visiting Soviet delegation turning into the courtyard just to look at it.

The courtyard belongs to the newspaper, not to a park. The reader who sent it tells us the tree can be seen from the pavement on Le Thai To, the street along the west shore of Hoan Kiem Lake. Since September 2026 the paper has also held free evening shows beneath it, with light projected onto the trunk. If you know which banyan species it is, tell us.
trees.how_to_recognise: The huge old banyan rising over the courtyard of the Nhan Dan newspaper building, between Hang Trong and Le Thai To on the west side of Hoan Kiem Lake; its crown shows from the Le Thai To pavement.
verified_sources: A reader's tip through the app, 2026-11-15
trees.verify_notes: 2026-11-16: tipped by a reader in the app (submission 700, 'Over 400 year old tree, a beloved landmark', with a Google Maps link to 'Cay da toa bao Nhan dan, 12 P. Le Thai To'). Earlier blocked as a lead (courtyard of a newspaper HQ, hard rule 10). The reader answered our question by mail on 2026-11-16: 'visible from the sidewalk', which clears it under Hidde's 2026-11-04 ruling (El Pino: clearly seen from public ground). Age: 'hon 300 tuoi' in Nhan Dan 23 Feb 2022 (author's claim, no basis) and 10 Mar 2026, and VietnamPlus Sep 2026 ('cay da hon 300 nam tuoi'); reader says over 400. Size: 'hang chuc nguoi om moi xue' (Nhan Dan 2022), no girth or height published. History: Nhan Dan 19 Aug 2021 (Dang Minh Phuong): paper moved from Son Tay 14 Oct 1954, to 71 Hang Trong about ten days later; site of Vu Tong Phan's school, later French villa (deputy governor-general's residence, Gauthier villa); Soviet delegation came in to look at the tree. Tan Da Show, free, 3D mapping on the tree, first 19 Sep 2026 (VietnamPlus). Species not named in any source: genus only, asked on the page. Pin: on the Le Thai To pavement beside the building (OSM relation 21394540, bbox 21.02923-21.03032, 105.85027-105.85117); trunk position in the courtyard unknown, so approximate.
trees.access: The courtyard belongs to the Nhan Dan newspaper and is not a public garden; the tree can be seen from the pavement on Le Thai To (a reader's account). Free evening shows are sometimes held beneath it.
